answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the dune hash is checked against the ocean checkpoint at intake, the knoll audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 5 epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
